paragraphs.source_en: Seated before Lady Sena was Ōga Yashirō, who had only that spring been appointed an accounts officer. paragraphs.source_en: On the sixth day of the fifth month, Ieyasu returned to the capital from Kanegasaki, and on the eighteenth he reached Hamamatsu. He did not visit Lady Sena after his return, driving her morbid jealousy to still greater frenzy. Yet Ieyasu would remain in Hamamatsu only briefly. Within a month he was to take the field in Ōmi, and the need to ready provisions, horses, and men left him not a moment to spare.
